scope.description: A figurative painting direction that places the user's requested subject within a compressed spatial frame, then applies restrained local contour shifts and visible overpainting to create tension. The frame can be a transparent architectural outline, platform, opening, or crop, but it must not become a literal cage by default. The subject remains identifiable and the paint process stays visible without imposing a fixed narrative.
limitations: Only use a figure or object supplied by the user; do not add a person, animal, portrait, or body part by default.
Keep any contour shift localized and recover the requested subject's identity and count.
Use enclosure and dark or saturated fields only when they fit the requested setting; do not add violence, screaming, crosses, arenas, or meat imagery.

pillars: Compress space around the existing subject with a spare frame or shallow architectural cue rather than a fully described room.
Apply small, selective contour displacements through dragged, scraped, or overpainted marks while preserving recognition.
Contrast a few broad color fields with visible changes in paint thickness and exposed underlying layers.
Keep areas of visual quiet so distortion reads as a deliberate pressure point, not all-over glitch.

rules.applies_when: The user supplies a figure or object for a psychologically tense painted scene.
rules.instruction: Place the requested subject in a compressed, shallow setting and use one spare frame, opening, platform, or boundary line to establish spatial pressure; do not add literal bars or a cage unless requested.
rules.observable: A simple spatial cue encloses or focuses the subject without building a detailed room or changing the user's setting.
rules.reject_when: The subject is replaced, the room becomes a generic prison, or the frame obscures essential anatomy or object structure.
rules.avoid: default cage bars, generic cell, and elaborate unrelated interior

rules.applies_when: The user requests expressive distortion of a recognizable subject.
rules.instruction: Choose one or two existing contours of the requested subject and offset or drag a short segment by a clearly visible amount; preserve the subject's identity, count, pose, and at least one clean recognition anchor. Keep the disturbance local rather than deforming every edge.
rules.observable: At ordinary viewing size, at least one localized contour shift is unmistakable while the requested subject and its parts remain countable and recognizable.
rules.reject_when: No contour shift is visible at ordinary viewing size, the subject's count or identity changes, features melt indiscriminately, or distortion becomes a digital glitch effect.
rules.avoid: all-over liquefaction, duplicate features, and grotesque default expression
